questions.text: Symptom Checker / AI Transparency: Disclose nature of automated advice: (1) Clear disclaimer (Not a doctor?); (2) Source of clinical protocols (WHO, National Guidelines?); (3) Accuracy rates / limitations; (4) Explanation of triage logic (Why go to hospital?); (5) Last update date of clinical content; (6) AI vs Rule-based distinction.
questions.evidence_required: User interface screenshots (disclaimers), Clinical protocol references, Algorithm validation reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Users may confuse AI with a real doctor. Must be explicit. Protocols must match local guidelines (e.g., Malaria treatment).

questions.text: Triage & Referral Logic: Explain referral decisions: (1) Criteria for referral (danger signs); (2) Facility selection logic (nearest vs best?); (3) Cost implications of referral; (4) Transparency on referral fees (kickbacks?); (5) Emergency vs non-emergency distinction.
questions.evidence_required: Triage protocols, Referral logic documentation, Conflict of interest policy (referral fees)
questions.africa_specific_notes: Referral kickbacks common. Users need to trust the referral is for their health, not profit. Danger signs must be clear.

questions.text: Prescription Logic Transparency: Explain drug recommendations: (1) Generic vs Brand name preference; (2) Contraindication warnings; (3) Side effect disclosure; (4) Dosage instructions clarity; (5) Source of drug information; (6) Interaction warnings.
questions.evidence_required: Prescription module logic, Drug database source, User information leaflets
questions.africa_specific_notes: Over-prescription of antibiotics is a crisis. Logic should favor national standard treatment guidelines.

questions.text: Consultation & Service Fees: Clear cost disclosure: (1) Upfront consultation fee; (2) Follow-up costs (included or extra?); (3) Hidden fees (platform fee, data fee); (4) Insurance coverage clarity (co-pay?); (5) Refund policy for missed appointments; (6) Payment methods accepted.
questions.evidence_required: Pricing page/screen, Refund policy, Insurance integration docs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Patients fear hidden costs. Upfront clarity essential. Insurance co-pays often confusing.

questions.text: Medication Pricing Transparency: Clear drug costs: (1) Itemized drug prices; (2) Delivery fees; (3) Comparison with reference prices (if available); (4) Generic substitution options (cheaper alternatives); (5) Total cost before checkout.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drugs are a major expense. Generic options must be shown to improve affordability.

questions.text: Patient Data Usage & Sharing: Who sees the data: (1) Doctor access scope; (2) Sharing with insurers (diagnosis codes?); (3) Sharing with employers (never?); (4) Sharing with government (mandatory reporting?); (5) Anonymization for research; (6) User consent granularity.
questions.evidence_required: Privacy policy (simplified), Consent forms, Data sharing agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Stigma (HIV, TB, Mental Health) is a major barrier. Fear of employer/community finding out. Explicit consent needed.

questions.text: Data Ownership & Portability: User rights: (1) Can user download their record?; (2) Can user transfer to another doctor?; (3) Can user delete their account (right to be forgotten)?; (4) Data retention period; (5) Access by family members (proxy access).
questions.evidence_required: Data export feature, Account deletion process, Proxy access policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: Patients often locked in. Portability allows continuity of care. Family access needed for elderly/children.

questions.text: Provider Credential Verification: Is the doctor real: (1) Display of license number; (2) Display of qualifications/specialty; (3) Verification status (verified by platform?); (4) Photo ID; (5) Years of experience; (6) Current physical practice location.
questions.evidence_required: Provider profile screens, Verification badge logic, License display
questions.africa_specific_notes: Quackery (fake doctors) is rampant. Platform must verify and display credentials clearly.

questions.text: Pharmacy/Facility Legitimacy: Is the pharmacy real: (1) Pharmacy Board license display; (2) Physical address verification; (3) Pharmacist-in-charge name; (4) Operating hours; (5) Contact details.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Illegal pharmacies sell fake/expired drugs. License display builds trust.

scoring_notes: Layer 2 (Transparency) for Healthcare in SSA: Clinical logic transparency prevents confusion between AI and doctors. Pricing transparency builds trust. Provider credential verification is a safety requirement against quacks.
